text:
Maya Park: FYI bringing up the new v3-small-int4 on the multilingual suite and hit a weird locale-specific regression on zh->en. BLEU on nightly dropped from 6.2 -> 5.1 after the quant pipeline. I traced a handful of failures to token boundary changes around emoji + short latin fragments followed by CJK (e.g., `hello🙂你好`).

Jin Lee: can you paste a minimal repro? sounds like tokenizer detok mismatch, or the quant step mutated tokenizer artifacts. :thinking:

Maya Park: repro below. Running our standard eval harness on a small subset: 
```
python -m evals.run --model redwood/v3-small-int4 --lang zh-en --subset bugset_emoji --batch 32
```
Example pair where we see difference: src: `今天我去看电影 hello🙂你好`
- golden decode (fp16): `I went to the movies today, hello 🙂 hello`
- quant decode (int4): `I went to the movies today, hello🙂你好`

I dumped token ids and detok: 
```
# fp16 tokens: [1012, 550, 2231,  ... , 3045, 1299] -> tokens: ['I', ' ', 'went', ..., 'hello', ' ', '🙂']
# int4 tokens: [1012, 550, 2231, ... , 3045, 1299, 3021] -> tokens: ['I', ' ', 'went', ..., 'hello', '🙂', '你好']
```
Notice the int4 path produced an extra token boundary merging latin+emoji with following CJK which changes downstream attention and generation.

Oliver Chen: that's helpful. Two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenizer normalization (unicode NFD/NFC or strip accents) was toggled in the tokenization config used during quant conversion; 2) the quantized runtime uses a different byte-to-unicode mapping shim for fast tokenizers (we had one bug previously where non-BMP emoji joined next codepoint).

Sam R: could also be the fallback unknown token handling when prefix cache is trimmed during continuous batching. If the KV cache slicing is off-by-one, the runtime might re-scan bytes across a boundary and produce different tokenization. I saw similar with combining marks across BPE joins. :bug:

Jin Lee: quick check i ran locally on that exact input with the HF fast tokenizer (pre- and post-quant) and got slightly different encodes. Dump: 
```
# pre-quant encode: [215, 874, 990, 4521, 3045, 1299]  # emoji separated
# post-quant encode: [215, 874, 990, 4521, 3045, 1299, 780]  # extra CJK piece
```
Looks like the tokenizer artifact is present before model forward for the quant build on the CI image. So maybe the converter replaced tokenizer files or packaging missed the `tokenizer.json` merge table.

Maya Park: hmm packaging would explain it. The int4 conversion step runs in a container that pulls artifacts from s3://releases/model-artifacts/v3-small-int4/{checkpoint,tokenizer.json,merges.txt}. I will diff the two tokenizer.json files from fp16 vs int4 build.

eval-bot: job 29822 created: nightly/multilang/emoji-boundary-sweep (subset=bugset_emoji) - started 

Oliver Chen: also check byte-level normalization flags in the tokenizer config (`add_prefix_space`, `normalize_unicode`, `strip_accents`) — small differences cause token joiners for mixed-script inputs. If tokenizer.json differs, that will definitely explain deterministic detok diffs.

Sam R: If we confirm a tokenizer packaging bug, quick mitigation: pin the hosted routing to fp16 for zh/en until we ship a patched package. We can also add an offline unit test that encodes a caselist of mixed-script lines and asserts identical token id sequences across builds. I'll add the test to evals/tests/tokenization_regressions.py.

Jin Lee: i ran a full encode-diff across 1k samples and attached a small diff snippet: 
```
- input: "... hello🙂你好 ..."
- fp16 ids:  [..., 3045, 1299, 999]
- int4 ids:  [..., 3045, 1299, 780]  # 780 is merged CJK token
```
I'll upload the full dump to s3://redwood-debug/1893456789/encode_diffs.tar.gz and kick off a deeper CI job that reproduces model outputs with the exact tokenizer files.

Maya Park: next steps: (1) I will diff tokenizer.json + merges.txt between fp16 and int4 artifacts and post results here; (2) Jin will run the sweep job and collect failing examples (priority); (3) Oliver will check converter script for any side effects on tokenizer packaging; (4) Sam adds the unit test and a temporary routing pin. ETA EOD. :eyes:

Oliver Chen: noted. If converter mutated anything we should also check release notes — maybe a dependency upgrade changed default normalization. I'll grep the converter diff for `tokenizer.json` ops.

Maya Park: update: found that int4 artifact build used an older tokenizers wheel in the container (0.12.x) vs the fp16 image which used 0.13.x. The older wheel writes `tokenizer.json` without the `normalizer` block for some mixed-script edge cases. That matches the encoding diffs. Uploading the diff now.

Jin Lee: nice catch. That explains it. I'll keep the CI sweep running and start rerunning the quant conversion inside the newer wheel in a repro branch.

Sam R: I'll land the test and add a temporary rule in the rollout policy to route zh-* to fp16 for 24h. After we re-run conversion + sweep and get parity we can remove the pin. :+1:

Maya Park: thanks all — will post the tokenizer diff link and the failing sample list once the jobs finish. If anyone sees other mixed-script cases (arabic + emoji + cjk), add them to bugset_emoji so we cover all boundaries.
